output.name: Halveth
output.myth: When a fisher is drowned, his widow flies the Split-Tail on the first calm day. It is a kite with two long tails, and they never pull together. One is for the house she keeps, the other for the man who went out in the boat. Ennu cut the first one from his own shirt, and Tavo came down the cliff laughing to tear it, but it would not tear, because grief is heavier than any gale. Tavo let it go, and it climbed. Hesk wound some slack into the string, which is why the tails reach so far: one goes south to the Lamp Kite, where lost boats steer by its light, and one goes east toward the Single Mitten, the red glove Tavo stole, still hunting its pair. The Down-Mother, to the north, keeps them warm. The widow ties her knot where the tails part, and lets out line until her hands go numb. She does not cut the string; Aun did that once and it was enough. She winds the kite home, mends her nets, and leaves the tails hanging on the peg.
output.finding: Find the Ringed Cod (Skéral) in the Spindle, then look about two-thirds of a hand-span east of it for the Split-Tail, Halveth.
